question: The rendered invocation is the kind's default, 'Append phases to `simple-login.integration` per hsdd/management/2026-10-31-intake-prd-simple-login-v2.md', which names no phase, while the step's queue item Q-086 (accepted by DEC-222) asks for the unshipped simple-login.integration.3 to be rewritten in place, and append mode allows a rewrite only when the invoking prompt names the phase. Rewrite simple-login.integration.3 in place, append a new phase, or append nothing?

options.label: rewrite simple-login.integration.3 in place
options.consequence: Does what Q-086 and DEC-222 accepted this step for; the phase keeps its id, name, tier, size, gate, Consumes and Dependencies, and only the stale sentence in Scope (b) changes. Reads the queue item the dispatch's front matter names as the instruction that names the phase, as DEC-210 did for S24.

options.label: append simple-login.integration.6
options.consequence: Follows the invocation's wording literally, but a phase cannot correct another phase's Scope; integration.3 would still reach its OpenSpec cycle with the false sentence, and the new phase would have no work of its own.

options.label: append nothing and explain
options.consequence: Leaves integration.3's Scope naming a drained request entry, a fallback the producer's answer closed, and rooms created in the database, which booking-api@v1's Development address contradicts.

why: The step exists for this rewrite: S26 routed Q-086 naming simple-login.integration.3 and asking for an in-place rewrite that keeps its id, and DEC-222 accepted it. The dispatch's front matter names Q-086 as this step's queue item; the invocation line is the phase-plan-append template's default and carries no insert-step text, so it says nothing either way about phase 3. simple-login.integration.3 has no verification doc on main (only integration.1 and .2 do; the conventions name no other main line), so it is unshipped and append mode may rewrite it. A verification doc for simple-login.integration.3 on main would have ruled the rewrite out.
evidence: git ls-tree main hsdd/verify/ (no simple-login.integration.3 doc)

question: Besides the pending section's emission line, which append mode requires and a later reconcile drains, does the plan's prose under the summary table also get a short paragraph naming the rewrite of simple-login.integration.3?

options.label: a rewrite paragraph under the table and the emission line
options.consequence: The plan keeps a lasting record of why phase 3's Scope (b) changed after its first append, as the plan already does for Update 1 and PRD v2 and as S24 did for simple-login.backend.7; a few lines more in the plan, none of which reaches the phase context.

options.label: the emission line only
options.consequence: The minimum append mode asks for; once a reconcile drains the pending section, the rewrite is visible only in git history.

chosen: a rewrite paragraph under the table and the emission line
why: The prose under the table is where this plan records each change to its phases (Update 1, PRD v2), and the emission line is replaced by a 'Reconciled' stamp the next time hsdd-reconcile runs on this node, so it is not a lasting record. hsdd-config injects only the phase section into the phase context, so the paragraph costs the implementer nothing. S24's rewrite of simple-login.backend.7 took the same form, which keeps the two nodes' plans alike. A rule in append mode limiting the prose under the table to appended phases would have made the emission line alone the choice.
evidence: hsdd-phase-plan SKILL.md Append Mode, Phase Summary Table
hsdd/spec/simple-login.integration.md Phase Plan prose (Update 1, PRD v2 paragraphs)
git show 14073d3 (S24's rewrite paragraph in hsdd/spec/simple-login.backend.md)

question: Q-086: 'Nothing the phase implements, consumes or replays changes, so no pending entry is expected ... the step decides that.' Does the rewrite of simple-login.integration.3 emit a `confirm`, `note`, `amend` or `request`, or only a new emission date line naming the rewrite?

options.label: emission line only
options.consequence: The line names the rewrite and says why it carries no entry; with no entry there is nothing for a reconcile to apply, which matches DEC-222's choice of no reconcile after this step.

options.label: re-confirm booking-api@v1 consumers
options.consequence: Restates what booking-api@v1's front matter already holds (simple-login.integration.3 among its consumers, `phase_ids: final`); a no-op entry that would need a reconcile DEC-222 did not insert.

options.label: note on the Local database conventions
options.consequence: Would restate that the service creates its tables in `meeting_rooms_e2e` when it starts, which hsdd/conventions.md Local database already says, citing booking-api@v1's Development address.

why: The rewrite changes no contract the phase consumes, no phase id, no shared artifact or package and no conventions fact: it states booking-api@v1's Development address, which S21 already folded into the contract (Versioning, 2026-11-01), and hsdd/conventions.md Local database already says the global setup re-creates `meeting_rooms_e2e` and the service creates its tables there. integration.3 is already in booking-api@v1's consumers with phase_ids final, so a confirm would change nothing. A change to what the phase consumes or replays, or a fact the conventions lack, would have needed an entry and a reconcile.
evidence: hsdd/contract/booking-api.md front matter, Development address, Versioning 2026-11-01
hsdd-phase-plan SKILL.md Governance Freeze, Append Mode

question: S27 rewrote integration.3's Scope (b) in place under Q-086 (again with the template's default invocation), left an emission line with no entry, and read the backend's D3 and S24's diff in a sibling's Phase Plan to check the rooms claim and the paragraph format. Keep the output or rework?

options.label: Keep the output
options.consequence: integration.3's Scope now matches booking-api@v1's Development address; the sibling read is declared and the new sentence cites only the contract.

options.label: Rework without the sibling read
options.consequence: The rooms correction would rest on the contract alone, which already states it; the sentence would be the same.

why: The change is one sentence, true against booking-api@v1, which the sentence cites; checking a claim against D3 did not put a sibling's internals into this plan. The sibling read is the second planner-isolation slip of the run (S18 was the first), recorded for the owner. A sentence citing the backend's plan would have changed this.
